s0101.literal: Wu prefecture inspector Chen Xiang led troops to attack Di; Xiang's army was greatly defeated; Marquis of Qianhua Chen Xu and Chenliu prefect Zhang Sui both died in battle; thereupon Di's host revived.
s0101.idiomatic: Wu prefect Chen Xiang marched against Di and was routed. Marquis of Qianhua Chen Xu and Chenliu prefect Zhang Sui fell in battle, and Di's forces rallied again.

s0102.literal: Emperor Wen sent area commander Cheng Lingxi to defeat them; Di again fled into mountain caves with more than ten men; days and months passed and those who followed him gradually grew weary.
s0102.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent area commander Cheng Lingxi to break them. Di fled into the hills with a dozen men. Time wore on, and even his companions began to suffer.

s0103.literal: Later he sent men out secretly to buy fish at Linchuan commandery market; his feet ached and he lodged with a village man; the villager reported to Linchuan prefect Luo Ya; Ya seized him and ordered him to bring Di in to redeem himself.
s0103.idiomatic: Later he sent men secretly to buy fish at the Linchuan market. His feet pained him, and he stayed with a villager, who told Linchuan prefect Luo Ya. Ya seized him and ordered him to deliver Di alive.

s0104.literal: He then sent loyal brave warriors to follow into the mountains, lure Di out hunting, and set ambush along the road; they beheaded him, sent the head to the capital, and exposed it at Vermilion Bird Observatory for three days.
s0104.idiomatic: He sent trusted warriors into the hills to lure Di out hunting, ambushed him on the road, and beheaded him. The head went to the capital and hung three days at Vermilion Bird Observatory.

s0105.literal: Liu Yi was a man of Changshan in Dongyang.
s0105.idiomatic: Liu Yi came from Changshan in Dongyang.

s0106.literal: His family for generations were a prominent surname of the commandery.
s0106.idiomatic: For generations his clan ranked among the commandery's leading families.

s0107.literal: Yi was skilled at deportment; his speech urbane and refined; he was a local strongman.
s0107.idiomatic: Yi carried himself well and spoke with polished ease; he was a local magnate.

s0108.literal: He gathered many ruffians, bullied poor and lowly; magistrates all feared him.
s0108.idiomatic: He gathered ruffians and bullied the poor; every magistrate feared him.

s0109.literal: In Liang times he was garrison chief at Xiepu and served as magistrate of Jin'an and Angu.
s0109.idiomatic: Under Liang he was garrison chief at Xiepu and magistrate of Jin'an and Angu in turn.

s0110.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled he returned to his home district and recruited soldiers; the Dongyang commandery aide had a feud with Yi and led troops to execute him and his wife and children.
s0110.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled he went home and raised troops. The Dongyang commandery aide, who hated him, led soldiers to kill Yi and his family.

s0111.literal: Prefect Shen Xun went to aid the capital and yielded the commandery to Yi; Yi had his nephew Chao oversee commandery affairs and led troops following Xun to the capital.
s0111.idiomatic: Prefect Shen Xun went to relieve the capital and yielded the commandery to Yi. Yi set his nephew Chao to run the commandery and marched with Xun to the capital.

s0112.literal: When the capital fell Yi followed Prince of Lincheng Xiao Dalian; Dalian commissioned him marshal and entrusted him with military affairs.
s0112.idiomatic: When the capital fell Yi followed Prince of Lincheng Xiao Dalian, who made him marshal and gave him the army.

s0113.literal: Yi's nature was cruel and violent, without far-reaching plans; he pressed Dalian's army commanders and used his intimates to build personal power—all resented him.
s0113.idiomatic: Yi was cruel and shortsighted; he squeezed Dalian's commanders and used favorites to build private power, and all hated him.

s0114.literal: When Jing's general Song Zixian crossed the Zhe River Yi fled home and soon surrendered his host to Zixian.
s0114.idiomatic: When Hou Jing's general Song Zixian crossed the Zhe, Yi fled home and soon surrendered his troops to him.

s0115.literal: Dalian also was hurrying to Dongyang's Xin'an Ridge intending to go to Poyang; Yi then guided Zixian and had him seize Dalian.
s0115.idiomatic: Dalian was also hurrying toward Xin'an Ridge in Dongyang, bound for Poyang. Yi guided Zixian and had him seize Dalian.

s0116.literal: Hou Jing appointed Yi Dongyang prefect and took his wife and children as hostages.
s0116.idiomatic: Hou Jing made Yi Dongyang prefect and held his wife and children hostage.

s0117.literal: Jing's field secretariat Liu Shenmao raised righteousness against Jing; Yi outwardly joined Shenmao but secretly was pledged to Jing.
s0117.idiomatic: Jing's field secretariat chief Liu Shenmao turned against him. Yi pretended to join Shenmao but secretly kept faith with Jing.

s0118.literal: When Shenmao was defeated Jing executed him; Yi alone escaped.
s0118.idiomatic: When Shenmao was beaten Jing killed him; Yi alone was spared.

s0119.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified Wang Sengbian sent Yi to comfort Dongyang; he still mustered home districts and held rugged passes; his band was very strong and prefectures and commanderies feared him.
s0119.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was crushed Wang Sengbian sent Yi to reassure Dongyang, but Yi still rallied the countryside and held the passes. His following was huge, and the region feared him.

s0120.literal: Emperor Yuan made him magistrate of Xin'an.
s0120.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan made him magistrate of Xin'an.

s0121.literal: When Jingzhou fell Wang Sengbian made him Dongyang prefect.
s0121.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell Wang Sengbian made him Dongyang prefect.

s0122.literal: When Emperor Wen pacified Kuaiji Yi though forwarded grain rations still monopolized a whole commandery—authority and favor were his alone.
s0122.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took Kuaiji, Yi sent grain but still kept the whole commandery in his grip, with power and favor his alone.

s0123.literal: Shaotai year 2, for supporting-joining merit, appointed bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, trust-military general, inspector of Jingzhou, concurrently Dongyang prefect, enfeoffed marquis of Yongxing county, [7] fief five hundred households.
s0123.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2, for aiding the court, he was made bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, trust-military general, inspector of Jingzhou with concurrent Dongyang prefect, and marquis of Yongxing county [7] with a fief of five hundred households. On [7]: the Southern History reads Yongjia.

s0124.literal: That year he was promoted to scattered-cavalry regular attendant and trust-prestige general; the fief increased by three hundred households; the rest remained as before.
s0124.idiomatic: That year he rose to scattered-cavalry regular attendant and trust-prestige general, with three hundred more households in the fief; other posts were unchanged.

s0125.literal: Also Emperor Wen's eldest daughter Princess Feng'an was matched to Yi's third son Zhenchen.
s0125.idiomatic: Emperor Wen also gave his eldest daughter, Princess Feng'an, to Yi's third son Zhenchen.

s0126.literal: Yongding year 2 he was summoned as bearer of credentials, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou military affairs, pacify-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou; Yi delayed and would not come.
s0126.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 he was summoned as bearer of credentials, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou, pacify-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou. Yi stalled and never came.

s0127.literal: Of old the four crimes were hard to pardon—Great Gun had none the Great Regulator spared; the Nine Li corrupted virtue—Shaohao surely executed them.
s0127.idiomatic: Of old the four crimes were hard to spare: Great Gun found no pardon from the Great Regulator; the Nine Li corrupted virtue, and Shaohao surely put them to death.

s0128.literal: Since antiquity emperors and kings have not coveted campaigns; when a man is the age's pest, affairs leave no choice.
s0128.idiomatic: Since antiquity kings have not loved war; when a man is the age's pest, they act because they must.

s0129.literal: The rebel Yi should many times have perished; he has mustered armor and gathered forces for years.
s0129.idiomatic: The rebel Yi should long since have perished; for years he has kept armor bright and hosts gathered.

s0130.literal: Advancing he declined the assembled dragons yet leaped a thousand li; retreating he harbored the rat's two minds and always held a hundred hearts.
s0130.idiomatic: Coming forward he refused the court's grace yet sprang a thousand li; drawing back he played the wavering rat and kept a hundred schemes.

s0131.literal: In mid-years he secretly pledged Panyu; the heavenly net was already spread wide and he was granted titles and names, bound by a state marriage—if only he would heed the call he might still change his face.
s0131.idiomatic: In mid-life he secretly tied himself to Panyu. The court spread the heavenly net, gave him rank and a princess marriage—had he listened, he might still have turned his face.

s0132.literal: Wang Lin seized the middle reaches and in turn answered him; he opened another southern route over the ranges and made himself sole host of the eastern road, clinging to vicious chiefs and rejoicing only in turmoil.
s0132.idiomatic: Wang Lin held the middle Yangtze and answered him in turn. He opened another mountain route south and made himself master of the eastern road, clinging to villains and welcoming chaos.

s0133.literal: Once the evil vapors were swept away his spirit flagged and his heart stood alone—like a wounded bird at the bowstring, like a cornered beast planning a desperate strike.
s0133.idiomatic: When the rebels were crushed his spirit sank and he stood alone—like a bird still flinching at the bow, like a beast at bay planning one last rush.

s0134.literal: Though again he sent his family as hostages, Ziyang's manner grew only fiercer;
s0134.idiomatic: Though he again sent his family as hostages, his manner grew only fiercer, like Ziyang;

s0135.literal: when the hostage son returned to court Wei Xiao's heart burned only hotter.
s0135.idiomatic: and when the hostage son returned to court his heart burned hotter still, like Wei Xiao.

s0136.literal: We are minded to nurture mutual completion, not counting faults and flaws, opening breast and loosening belt, earnestly instructing.
s0136.idiomatic: We meant to nurture him to completion, overlooking every fault, opening our breast and speaking with all earnestness.

s0137.literal: His owl eyes shone clearer; his owl cry never changed; he then set troops at the river mouth and strict guards below Huai—open rebellion that could not be hidden.
s0137.idiomatic: His owl eyes shone the brighter; his owl cry never changed. He set troops at the river mouth and strict guards below the Huai—open rebellion that could not be concealed.

s0138.literal: Moreover Jing prefecture is rich soil and south of Kuaiji broad and populous; he forever cut off royal tax and long choked the people; fine bamboo and good timber never reached the capital carriage; petty reeds-and-rushes bandits together indulged greedy cruelty—thinking of those remaining folk doubles our sigh.
s0138.idiomatic: Jing was rich land and south Kuaiji teemed with people, yet he forever withheld the royal tax and choked the folk. Fine bamboo never reached the capital; petty bandits plundered with him. To think of those who remained is to sigh twice.

s0139.literal: Western Rong bent the knee and came in at the heavy passes; Qin submitted to the wind and together yielded invaded lands; the three marches are already at peace and the four quarters all secure—only this petty demon should be swept away.
s0139.idiomatic: Western tribes knelt at the passes; Qin came over and returned seized lands; the three marches are quiet and the four quarters secure—only this petty demon should be destroyed.

s0140.literal: Let bearer of credentials, commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou military affairs, campaign-north general, minister of works, inspector of South Xuzhou, and founding duke of Guiyang commandery Andu go to seize and execute; guilt rests on Yi alone; the rest are not questioned.
s0140.idiomatic: Let bearer of credentials, commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou, campaign-north general, minister of works, inspector of South Xuzhou, and founding duke of Guiyang Andu go to seize and kill him. Guilt rests on Yi alone; no one else will be punished.

s0141.literal: Yi had expected the government army to come up the Qiantang River; Andu instead marched overland through Kuaiji and Zhuji to strike him.
s0141.idiomatic: Yi expected the imperial army up the Qiantang. Andu marched overland through Kuaiji and Zhuji instead.

s0142.literal: When Yi heard the army had come he was greatly afraid, abandoned the commandery, and fled to Taozhi Ridge; at the pass mouth he set palisades to hold firm.
s0142.idiomatic: Hearing the army had come, Yi was terrified, left the commandery, and fled to Taozhi Ridge, where he walled the pass.

s0143.literal: Next spring Andu greatly broke his palisades; Yi and his second son Chuxin fled to Chen Baoying; his remaining partisans, men and women numbering several thousand, were captured.
s0143.idiomatic: Next spring Andu smashed the palisades. Yi and his second son Chuxin fled to Chen Baoying. Several thousand followers, men and women, were taken.

s0144.literal: Tianjia year 5, when Chen Baoying was pacified Yi was also seized and sent to the capital and beheaded in Jiankang market; sons, nephews, and fellow conspirators of every age were executed; only the third son Zhenchen was spared for having married the princess.
s0144.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 5, when Chen Baoying fell, Yi was seized, sent to the capital, and beheaded in the Jiankang market. Sons, nephews, and allies of every age were killed; only the third son Zhenchen was spared because he had married the princess.

s0145.literal: Chen Baoying was a man of Houguan in Jin'an.
s0145.idiomatic: Chen Baoying came from Houguan in Jin'an.

s0146.literal: His family for generations were one of the four great surnames of Min.
s0146.idiomatic: For generations his clan was one of Min's four great surnames.

s0147.literal: His father Yu had talent and ability and was a commandery strongman.
s0147.idiomatic: His father Yu was capable and a commandery magnate.

s0148.literal: Baoying's nature was changeable and full of shifting deceit.
s0148.idiomatic: Baoying was fickle and steeped in deceit.

s0149.literal: In Liang times Jin'an rebelled many times and repeatedly killed commandery chiefs; at first Yu together incited and completed the affair, then again served as guide for government troops to break them—thereafter all military power of the commandery issued from himself.
s0149.idiomatic: Under Liang Jin'an rose repeatedly and killed its prefects. Yu first stirred the rebels, then guided government troops to crush them, and from then on held the commandery's military power.

s0150.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled Jin'an prefect Marquis of Binhua Xiao Yun yielded the commandery to Yu; Yu was old and only handled commandery affairs, putting Baoying in charge of the army.
s0150.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Jin'an prefect Marquis of Binhua Xiao Yun yielded the commandery to Yu. Yu was old and ran civil affairs while Baoying commanded the troops.

s0151.literal: At that time the eastern lands were in famine; Kuaiji was worst; seven or eight in ten died; common men and women all sold themselves, yet Jin'an alone was rich and fertile.
s0151.idiomatic: The east was starving; Kuaiji was worst, with seven or eight in ten dead. Families sold themselves, yet Jin'an alone stayed rich.

s0152.literal: Baoying by sea raided Lin'an, Yongjia, Kuaiji, Yuyao, and Zhuji, [8] and also carried rice and grain to trade with them, gaining much silks, jades, and women; those who could bring boats also all fled to join him—thereby he amassed great wealth and his soldiers and masses were strong.
s0152.idiomatic: Baoying raided by sea at Linhai [8], Yongjia, Kuaiji, Yuyao, and Zhuji, and traded rice and grain for silks, jades, and women. On [8]: Lin'an in the base text should be Linhai. Whoever could sail a boat joined him, and he grew very rich and strong.

s0153.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified Emperor Yuan therefore made Yu Jin'an prefect.
s0153.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was crushed Emperor Yuan made Yu Jin'an prefect.

s0154.literal: Baoying married Liu Yi's daughter; when Hou Andu campaigned against Yi, Baoying sent troops to help and also supplied Zhou Di with grain and arms, raiding out at Linchuan.
s0154.idiomatic: Baoying married Liu Yi's daughter. When Hou Andu attacked Yi, Baoying sent troops to help and supplied Zhou Di with grain, then raided Linchuan.

s0155.literal: When area commander Zhang Zhaoda defeated Di at Dongxing and Nancheng, Emperor Wen then ordered Zhaoda to command all armies south over the ranges by the Jian'an road, and also ordered inspector of Yizhou and concurrent Xinyi prefect Yu Xiaoding to command armies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, and Yongjia from the east to join, to campaign against Baoying, and also ordered the director of imperial clan affairs to strike him from the genealogical register.
s0155.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhaoda beat Di at Dongxing and Nancheng, Emperor Wen put Zhaoda over all forces crossing south by the Jian'an road and ordered Yizhou inspector Yu Xiaoding, also Xinyi prefect, to strike from the east through Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, and Yongjia. The clan director was told to erase Baoying from the register.

s0156.literal: Thereupon the Masters of Writing issued a dispatch saying:
s0156.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing then issued a dispatch:

s0157.literal: To the gentry and commoners of Jin'an: of old Longxi's brigands resisted and Han did not delay punishment; Liaodong rebelled and changed allegiance and Wei set forth a great plan.
s0157.idiomatic: To the people of Jin'an: Longxi once resisted and Han did not delay punishment; Liaodong rebelled and Wei laid down a great plan.

s0158.literal: As for Wu Ru's merit under Han and Youhu's kinship under Xia—down to taking Wu Pi's son and bringing the armies of the Four Seas, defying Si Qi's command and incurring the punitive oath of Gan—
s0158.idiomatic: Wu Ru served Han; Youhu shared Xia's kinship; one took Wu Pi's son and raised the armies of the Four Seas; another defied Si Qi and met the oath of Gan—

s0159.literal: how much more when clan is not tied to the ancestral alliance and name is not recorded among ordinary vessels, yet plainly completing three rebellions and guilt reaching the four crimes?
s0159.idiomatic: how much more when a clan is not bound to the royal house, its name not listed among the worthy, yet plainly commits three rebellions and guilt as deep as the four crimes?

s0160.literal: We find the Min bandit Chen Baoying father and son—barbarian dress, branch offshoots—originally lost to love and respect.
s0160.idiomatic: We find the Min bandits Chen Baoying and his father—savage dress, a side branch—who from the first forgot love and respect.

s0161.literal: Liang's age fell into chaos; the Min corner was cut off; the father was bold and stirred the barbarian hills; with topknots and squatting like chiefs they heard no instruction in righteousness and relied on flattery and deceit, then suddenly let fall the seal.
s0161.idiomatic: Liang fell into chaos and Min was cut off. The father was bold and stirred the hill tribes; with topknots they sat as chiefs, knowing no rites, trusting only flattery, then cast off the seal.

s0162.literal: The Han line was ending; the net leaked even great fish; days and months rolled on and they were cast beyond the border.
s0162.idiomatic: The Han line was ending; the net let great fish through; time passed and they were left outside the law.

s0163.literal: Since the southeast's royal qi truly marked the holy foundation and the Dipper and Ox gathered stars truly matched the royal trace, though scaling mountains and crossing seas seemed like sincere submission, they privately cut off gems and jewels and in the end offered scant tribute.
s0163.idiomatic: Southeastern royal qi marked the new throne; Dipper and Ox stars matched the royal trace. Though they seemed to come over mountains and seas in submission, they kept gems for themselves and barely paid tribute.

s0164.literal: The court followed nurture and held forbearance; favor and glory were lofty and bright; he rose from home to govern a commandery with the glory of daytime brocade; land was split to set a province and the splendor of a frontier banner was lent.
s0164.idiomatic: The court nurtured and bore with them, heaping favor: from home to commandery with brocade glory by day; land split into a province and a commander's banner lent.

s0165.literal: At once households were enfeoffed and still enfeoffed at Liyang; ten men rode ornamented carriages while ten thousand stone salaries guarded humble huts.
s0165.idiomatic: Households were enfeoffed at once, with Liyang still in the fief; ten men rode fine carriages while ten-thousand-bushel pay guarded poor roofs.

s0166.literal: Again, as flourishing Han ruled all, favor was pushed as with Lou Jing; as grand Zhou held court Teng was made long marquis—thereby purple mud and blue paper bore favor from afar and district and village tortoise seals reached even infants.
s0166.idiomatic: As Han ruled all, favor spread like Lou Jing's; as Zhou held court Teng was made long marquis—purple edicts and blue paper came from afar, tortoise seals from district and village even to infants.

s0167.literal: From valley to tall tree, what could compare—yet he harbored poison and dared wolfish outrage.
s0167.idiomatic: From low to high, what could match it—yet he hid poison and dared wolfish outrage.

s0168.literal: He linked with Liu Yi inside and out with Zhou Di; oaths and marriage made them lip and teeth; strong in the mountain valleys they shifted with the years.
s0168.idiomatic: He joined Liu Yi and Zhou Di, oath and marriage making them lip and teeth, strong in the hills year after year.

s0169.literal: When our armed riders guarded the mountains and fixed the western part of Qinwang's outlook, and war-boats went down the rapids and took the southern streams of Huize, they then dared raise the axe and together aid the vicious brood—none failed to break at the bowstring and all the ugly crew were slaughtered.
s0169.idiomatic: When our cavalry held the mountains and took Qinwang's western flank, and war-boats swept Huize's southern streams, they still raised the axe to aid the rebels—every one broke at the string and the whole wicked band was killed.

s0170.literal: Each time guilt lay with the chiefs we pitied those driven on; captives taken were all ordered released in mercy.
s0170.idiomatic: Each time guilt lay with the chiefs we pitied those they drove; captives were ordered released.

s0171.literal: We still sent palace envoys and lowered edicts; the heavenly net was vast and still allowed change of mind.
s0171.idiomatic: We still sent palace envoys with edicts; the heavenly net was wide and still allowed repentance.

s0172.literal: Yi had already fled to peril and Di had escaped punishment; they deceived and insulted the king's men and made themselves a mountain lair—so Yuan Xi asked for a mat and sighed far off at Touxing's march, and Ma Yuan watched frogs yet was content in the well bottom.
s0172.idiomatic: Yi had fled to the hills and Di had escaped justice. They mocked the king's officers and made a mountain lair—like Yuan Xi asking for a mat and sighing at Touxing far away, like Ma Yuan watching frogs content in a well.

s0173.literal: As for cutting off the nine levies, plundering the four peoples, seizing all wealth within the borders and stripping every household, every bondservant was looted from the black-haired folk.
s0173.idiomatic: They cut off the nine taxes, plundered the four orders, seized all wealth in the region and stripped every house, and every bondservant was taken from the people.

s0174.literal: Bandits fanned one another in league and track; they again crossed beyond the ocean, raided Jia mouth, pressed the range passes, and stormed Shucheng, binding officials and people and burning government temples—if this may be indulged, what may not be borne?
s0174.idiomatic: Bandits stirred one another and again crossed the sea, raided Jia mouth, struck the passes, stormed Shucheng, bound officials and people, and burned government temples—if this is allowed, what is not?

s0175.literal: Now sent are Shazhou inspector Yu Wenjiong, bright-prestige general Cheng Wenji, acting bearer of credentials and fierce-assault general and Chengzou inspector Gan Ta, acting bearer of credentials and cloud-banner general Tan Zhen, acting bearer of credentials and fierce-assault general and former overseer of Linhai commandery Chen Sijing, vanguard general Xu Zhiyuan, bright-resolve general and founding marquis of Yihuang Huaiji, open-distance general and newly appointed Jin'an prefect Zhao Can, bearer of credentials and direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry and stalwart-military general and Dingzhou inspector and founding marquis of Kangle Lin Feng, acting bearer of credentials and trust-prestige general and commander-in-chief of eastern campaign military affairs and Yizhou inspector Yu Xiaoding—leading twenty thousand feathered guards, war-junks covering the sea, riding the blue waves to sweep the nest and den.
s0175.idiomatic: Now Shazhou inspector Yu Wenjiong, bright-prestige general Cheng Wenji, acting credential-bearer and fierce-assault general Gan Ta of Chengzou, acting credential-bearer and cloud-banner general Tan Zhen, acting credential-bearer and fierce-assault general Chen Sijing, former overseer of Linhai, vanguard general Xu Zhiyuan, bright-resolve general and founding marquis of Yihuang Huaiji, open-distance general and new Jin'an prefect Zhao Can, credential-bearer and direct regular attendant Lin Feng of Dingzhou, and acting credential-bearer Yu Xiaoding of Yizhou, commander of the eastern campaign, lead twenty thousand guards. War-junks cover the sea to sweep the nest clean.

s0176.literal: These all understand shame and teach war; at Ruxu they array troops, [9] repeatedly followed Yang Pu, often chased Sun En, cut the flood-dragon midstream and ordered Feng Yi to beat drums, took turtle and alligator for chariot and rolled over Fanghu to raise banners.
s0176.idiomatic: They know shame and teach war; at Ruxu they drill [9], followed Yang Pu again and again, chased Sun En repeatedly, cut the flood-dragon midstream and ordered Feng Yi to drum, drove turtle and alligator as chariot and raised banners over Fanghu. On [9]: the Ruxu camp reference is not corrupt.

s0177.literal: Yi'an prefect Zhang Shaobin, loyal and sincere in arrival, repeatedly sent asking for troops; Nankang interior administrator Pei Ji, newly appointed light-chariot general Liu Feng, and Donghengzhou inspector Qian Daozhi all at once sent men and arms to march with Shaobin.
s0177.idiomatic: Yi'an prefect Zhang Shaobin came in loyalty and begged for troops again and again. Nankang interior administrator Pei Ji, new light-chariot general Liu Feng, and Donghengzhou inspector Qian Daozhi all sent men and arms to march with him.

s0178.literal: The late minister of works Lord Ouyang in old days had a memorial asking to proclaim a limited campaign; across the distance his intent matched, like Fubo on warfare; long gone he left a testament, the same as Ziyan's "do not spare."
s0178.idiomatic: The late minister of works Lord Ouyang once memorialized for a limited campaign; his intent matched ours across the distance, like Fubo's talk of war. Dead, he left a charge like Ziyan's "do not spare."

s0179.literal: The campaign-south lord has died; the upper plan is not forgotten; Zhounan's remaining regret—the heir son will not fail it.
s0179.idiomatic: The campaign-south lord is gone, but the upper plan is not forgotten. Zhounan's remaining regret—the heir will not fail it.

s0180.literal: Guangzhou inspector Ouyang He fulfills the family name and follows the broad plan; river army and foot soldiers twenty thousand divide and hurry; on water he checks the long whale, on land he reins the great boar, leading Heng and Guang troops to join our six armies.
s0180.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Ouyang He keeps the family name and follows the broad plan. Twenty thousand men by river and land hurry forward; on water he blocks the long whale, on land he reins the great boar, leading Heng and Guang to join our six armies.

s0181.literal: Tongzhou inspector Li La, [10] Mingzhou inspector Dai Huang, Xinzhou inspector Qu Baishou, [11] stalwart-military general Xiu Xingshi, Chenliu prefect Zhang Sui, former Angu interior administrator Que Shen, former Luling prefect Lu Zilong, former Yuning prefect Ren Mannu, [12] Bashan prefect Huang Fahui, martial-display general and heir of the Duke of Xiangdong Xu Jingcheng, Wu prefect Lu Guangda, former Wu prefect and founding marquis of Suixing Xiang, bearer of credentials and commander-in-chief of campaign military affairs and scattered-cavalry regular attendant and protector general Zhaoda—leading five thousand brocade cavalry and twenty thousand mailed men, crossing straight at Shaowu and then encamping at Jin'an.
s0181.idiomatic: Tongzhou inspector Li La [10], Mingzhou inspector Dai Huang, Xinzhou inspector Qu Baishou [11], stalwart-military general Xiu Xingshi, Chenliu prefect Zhang Sui, former Angu interior administrator Que Shen, former Luling prefect Lu Zilong, former Yuning prefect Ren Mannu [12], Bashan prefect Huang Fahui, martial-display general and heir of Duke of Xiangdong Xu Jingcheng, Wu prefect Lu Guangda, former Wu prefect and founding marquis of Suixing Xiang, and credential-bearer Zhang Zhaoda, protector general and commander of the campaign, lead five thousand brocade cavalry and twenty thousand mailed men across at Shaowu and camp at Jin'an. On [10]: Li La is also written Ji La or Li Du, doubtful. On [11]: Baishou is probably Baihu (Tiger), a Tang taboo change. On [12]: Yuning, not Yuzhang, is correct here.

s0182.literal: Holding reins and raising banners, leveling mountains and filling valleys, they fix a date to pinch the corner and control those who flee.
s0182.idiomatic: Holding reins and raising banners, leveling mountains and filling valleys, they set a day to pinch the corner and catch the fugitives.

s0185.literal: [cheng] prefect Qian Su, [13] Linchuan prefect Luo Ya, left leader of the crown prince's guard Sun Xu, Xunyang prefect Mo Jinglong, and Yuzhang prefect Liu Guangde—all according to circumstance garrison and suppress, relays on the road.
s0185.idiomatic: Collation variant: [cheng]; adopted reading: Former Xuancheng prefect Qian Su [13], Linchuan prefect Luo Ya, left leader of the crown prince's guard Sun Xu, Xunyang prefect Mo Jinglong, and Yuzhang prefect Liu Guangde all garrison as occasion demands, relays on every road. On [13]: Zhou Di's biography reads Xuancheng for Xuanwei.

s0186.literal: Bearer of credentials, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacify-south general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Jiangzhou inspector, and founding marquis of Xinjian Fading—on alert midstream as rear guard.
s0186.idiomatic: Credential-bearer Huang Fading, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacify-south general with a mansion equal to the three dukes, Jiangzhou inspector, and founding marquis of Xinjian, stands alert midstream as rear guard.

s0187.literal: Where axe and halberd reach, guilt rests only on the chief villain and Liu Yi father and son.
s0187.idiomatic: Where the axe reaches, guilt rests only on the chief villain and Liu Yi and his son.

s0188.literal: Their party chiefs, though some begged mud at Hangu and turned their backs like Huaiyin, if they can suddenly change course and by the moment establish merit, not only will amnesty be granted,
s0188.idiomatic: Their chiefs, though some clung to Hangu or turned like Huaiyin, if they change course and win merit at once will not only be pardoned,

s0190.idiomatic: Collation variant: [still]; adopted reading: but also be promoted and rewarded.

s0191.literal: [14] The gentry and commoners of Jian and Jin long driven on—the great army will clearly comfort them; each secure in occupation; those displaced and lost to home return at once to native districts.
s0191.idiomatic: [14] The people of Jian and Jin long driven by force—the great army will comfort them plainly, each to his trade; those displaced return home.

s0192.literal: The rest for establishing merit are already set forth in the reward scale.
s0192.idiomatic: Other rewards for merit are already set out in the regulations.

s0193.literal: If they cling to error and do not change, share evil and hesitate, when axe and halberd come none will know pardon.
s0193.idiomatic: If they cling to error, share the crime, and hesitate, when the axe comes none will be spared.

s0194.literal: Zhaoda having already taken Di crossed Dongxing Ridge and encamped at Jian'an; Yu Xiaoding also from the Linhai road struck at Jin'an; Baoying held the lake margin at Jian'an and met the royal army in opposition, setting palisades by water and land.
s0194.idiomatic: Zhaoda, having beaten Di, crossed Dongxing Ridge and camped at Jian'an. Yu Xiaoding also struck Jin'an from the Linhai road. Baoying held the lake shore at Jian'an and met the royal army behind water and land palisades.

s0195.literal: Zhaoda dug deep moats and high ramparts and would not fight, only ordering soldiers to cut wood for rafts.
s0195.idiomatic: Zhaoda dug deep moats and high walls and would not fight, only ordering men to cut wood for rafts.

s0196.literal: Soon the water rose; riding the flood they released them, burst the water palisades, and then by water and foot closed in; Baoying's host collapsed; he himself fled into mountain grass, cornered and seized, and with his sons and younger brothers twenty men was sent to the capital and beheaded in Jiankang market.
s0196.idiomatic: Soon the water rose. They rode the flood, smashed the water palisades, and closed in by river and land. Baoying's army broke. He fled into the hills, was caught, and with twenty sons and younger brothers was sent to the capital and beheaded in the Jiankang market.

s0197.literal: The historian says: At the end of Liang calamity and bale rose together; chiefs of commanderies and cave-holds and heroes of village stockades, relying on plunder to grow strong, indulged bullying to become great.
s0197.idiomatic: The historian says: At Liang's end calamity bred rebels everywhere. Cave chiefs and stockade heroes grew strong by plunder and great by bullying.

s0198.literal: The Founder met the age, quelled disorder, and settled peace; Xiong Tanlang, Zhou Di, Liu Yi, and Chen Baoying though themselves met the rising fortune still set their hearts on disorder.
s0198.idiomatic: The Founder met the age, quelled disorder, and brought peace. Xiong Tanlang, Zhou Di, Liu Yi, and Chen Baoying met the rising fortune yet still chose rebellion.

s0199.literal: Tanlang's treachery turned again and again—his extermination was fortune indeed.
s0199.idiomatic: Tanlang's treachery turned again and again; to destroy him was fortune indeed.

s0200.literal: Baoying and Yi—Emperor Wen sometimes bound them by marriage or placed them among his kin; could he not have overawed them? It was rather that he wished to win them by virtue.
s0200.idiomatic: Baoying and Yi—Emperor Wen sometimes bound them by marriage or treated them as kin. Could he not have overawed them? He meant to win them by virtue.
